definition: Inferring the reward function that explains observed behavior, rather than assuming it is given.
details: Inferring the reward function that explains observed behavior, rather than assuming it is given. The conceptual ancestor of preference-based reward modeling: RLHF is, in effect, IRL from pairwise human comparisons.

explainer.lead: Inverse reinforcement learning infers the reward function that explains observed behaviour, rather than assuming the reward is given. It matters as the conceptual ancestor of preference-based reward modeling.

tiers.eli5: Instead of being told the rules of a game, you watch someone play and work out what they seem to be trying to score.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to recover objectives from demonstrations when the reward is unknown. RLHF is, in effect, IRL from pairwise human comparisons.
tiers.paperLevel: Inferring the reward function that explains observed behavior, rather than assuming it is given. No formal formula or stated limits beyond this.

explainer.example: Given demonstrations of a task, the method infers a reward function consistent with the observed actions instead of scoring them against a hand-specified reward.
